text:
The story around Matvei Michkov this fall is minutes, not goals. He is playing under 16 a night for Rick Tocchet, the headlines say he has sounded off about it, and on Nov. 11 Kevin Weekes reported that he wants "a new start elsewhere." We don't know where that ends. We do know what he has done with the ice he gets.

He has 10 goals in 20 games, the most on the team, and by our wins-added measure his goals have swung more games than all but 15 skaters in the league. Some of that is hot shooting: 34% on 29 shots, against a range near 15%. That will come down. But his own chances are up (1.04 expected goals per 60, from 0.84), his ice time over the last ten games is up two minutes, and he is now on for 76% of Philadelphia's power-play chances.

The five-on-five game is the soft spot: the Flyers get just 40.5% of expected goals with him out there. Our projection is about 29 goals. That is a player you build around, and it is why the minutes argument isn't going away.
headline: Michkov is scoring through the ice time fight
